title: Trapping Rain Water
description: Given n non-negative integers representing an elevation map where the width of each bar is 1, compute how much water it can trap after raining.
constraints: The solution should run in O(n) time
O(1) extra space is preferred but not enforced

examples.explanation: The elevation map traps 6 units of water between the bars.
The elevation map traps 9 units of water between the bars.

title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
description: Given two sorted arrays nums1 and nums2 of size m and n respectively, return the median of the two sorted arrays combined. The overall run time complexity should be O(log(m+n)). The result should be returned as a string representing a floating point number rounded to 5 decimal places.
constraints: The combined array is not guaranteed to have distinct elements

examples.explanation: The merged array is [1,2,3], and its median is 2.
The merged array is [1,2,3,4], and its median is (2+3)/2 = 2.5.

title: Sliding Window Maximum
description: Given an array of integers nums and a sliding window of size k which moves from the very left of the array to the very right, return an array of the maximum value in each window as it slides.
constraints: The solution should run in O(n) time using a deque-based approach

examples.explanation: The maximum values in each sliding window of size 3 are shown in order.
There is only one window containing a single element.

title: First Missing Positive
description: Given an unsorted integer array nums, return the smallest missing positive integer. You must implement an algorithm that runs in O(n) time and uses O(1) auxiliary space.
constraints: The algorithm must run in O(n) time
O(1) extra space must be used (in-place modification allowed)

examples.explanation: The numbers 1 and 2 are present, so the smallest missing positive integer is 3.
The number 1 is present but 2 is missing, so the answer is 2.

title: Maximum Sum of Two Non-Overlapping Subarrays
description: Given an integer array nums and two integers firstLen and secondLen, return the maximum sum of elements in two non-overlapping subarrays with lengths firstLen and secondLen. The subarrays can appear in either order relative to each other, but must not overlap.
constraints: The two subarrays must not overlap in index

examples.explanation: One optimal choice is subarrays [9] (length 1) and [6,5] (length 2), or similar combinations, summing to 20.
The optimal choice sums subarrays of length 3 and 2 that together total 29.
